tasks:
  callisto-status:
    command: "cargo run --bin callisto -- status"
    inputs:
      - ".changeset/**/*"
      - "callisto.toml"

  callisto-validate:
    command: "cargo run --bin callisto -- status --check"
    inputs:
      - ".changeset/**/*"
      - "callisto.toml"

  callisto-schema:
    command: "cargo run --bin callisto -- schema"
# Global tasks inherited by every project (all crates use the rust toolchain uniformly).
tasks:
  build:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["build", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  test:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["test", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "**/*.snap"
      - "**/*.trycmd"

  lint:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["clippy", "-p", "$project", "--all-targets", "--", "-D", "warnings"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["fmt", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format-check:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["fmt", "-p", "$project", "--", "--check"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  publish:
    command: "cargo"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"
    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true
    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: auto
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: fallback

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. if: needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix != '[]'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.hostRunner }}
    permissions: {contents: read, id-token: write, attestations: write}
    env:
      KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
      TRIPLE: ${{ matrix.triple }}
      USE_CROSS: ${{ matrix.useCross }}
      PACKAGE_DIR: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
      PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.packageName }}
      MANIFEST_PATH: ${{ matrix.manifestPath }}
      ASSET: ${{ matrix.artifactName }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {persist-credentials: false}
      - name: Install the Rust target
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rustup target add "$TRIPLE"
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then cargo install cross --locked --version 0.2.5; fi
      - name: Build the napi addon
        if: matrix.kind == 'napi'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--platform --release --target "$TRIPLE" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-out")
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then args+=(--use-cross); fi
          if [[ -n "$MANIFEST_PATH" ]]; then args+=(--manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$MANIFEST_PATH"); fi
          (cd "${PACKAGE_DIR:-.}" && npx --yes --package @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4 napi build "${args[@]}")
      - if: matrix.kind == 'napi'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: napi-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Build and archive the release artifact
        if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo_bin=cargo
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then cargo_bin=cross; fi
          cd "${PACKAGE_DIR:-.}"
          "$cargo_bin" build --release --locked --target "$TRIPLE" --package "$PACKAGE"
          metadata=$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1)
          target_dir=$(jq -r .target_directory <<< "$metadata")
          temp=$RUNNER_TEMP
          if command -v cygpath > /dev/null; then target_dir=$(cygpath -u "$target_dir"); temp=$(cygpath -u "$temp"); fi
          case "$TRIPLE" in *windows*) suffix=.exe ;; wasm32-*) suffix=.wasm ;; *) suffix= ;; esac
          stage="$temp/release-stage"
          out="$temp/release-assets"
          mkdir -p "$stage" "$out"
          jq -r --arg package "$PACKAGE" '.packages[] | select(.name == $package) | .targets[]
            | select(.kind | index("bin")) | .name' <<< "$metadata" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
            cp "$target_dir/$TRIPLE/release/$bin$suffix" "$stage/"
          done
          if [[ -z "$(ls -A "$stage")" ]]; then
            echo "::error::$PACKAGE builds no binary target for $TRIPLE"
            exit 1
          fi
          cd "$stage"
          case "$ASSET" in
            *.tar.gz | *.tgz) tar -czf "$out/$ASSET" ./* ;;
            *.tar.xz) tar -cJf "$out/$ASSET" ./* ;;
            *.zip) if command -v zip > /dev/null; then zip -q "$out/$ASSET" ./*; else 7z a -bd "$out/$ASSET" ./* > /dev/null; fi ;;
            *)
              binaries=(./*)
              if [[ ${#binaries[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
                echo "::error::$ASSET is not an archive name, but $PACKAGE builds ${#binaries[@]} binaries"
                exit 1
              fi
              cp "${binaries[0]}" "$out/$ASSET"
              ;;
          esac
      - if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/${{ matrix.artifactName }}
      - if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: asset-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  # No registry credentials: the executing job uploads these exact files.
  build-python:
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@__COMMIT__ # callisto@__VERSION__
        with: {version: callisto@__VERSION__}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Build the Python distributions
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet __BUILD__

---
callisto-cli: minor
---

A `pypi` registry in `callisto.toml` can set `publish-url` when its upload endpoint differs from its simple index: Callisto reads releases from `url` and uploads to `publish-url`. Without it, `url` serves both, as before.
--- .changeset/brave-stags-hunt.md
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

A release whose changelog exists but cannot be read now fails planning with E125 naming the file, instead of publishing generated notes in place of the changelog the release PR reviewed. A missing changelog, a missing version section and an empty section still fall back to generated notes, with the notice.
--- .changeset/jolly-otters-pounce.md
---
callisto-cli: minor
---

A Cargo workspace below the repository root, such as `native/` or `rust/`, is now supported. Its members inherit `version.workspace = true` and `{ workspace = true }` dependencies from it instead of failing with E313, `callisto version` refreshes and stages the `Cargo.lock` beside it, and a release commit is verified against it. Its own `members` and `exclude` decide which crates in it are packages.
--- .changeset/jolly-stags-swim.md
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

The interrupted-run check now finds a staged version bump in the Cargo workspace a package named at `HEAD` even when its working-tree manifest already names a different `package.workspace`.
--- .changeset/mighty-cobras-leap.md
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

A nested npm workspace that declares `workspaces` in its `package.json` and has no lockfile now publishes from its own directory, and a lockfile beside a package no longer takes it out of its workspace. `npm view` and a publish by directory run in that directory too, so the version looked for and the version published come from the same `.npmrc`. A package that moves to a different `package.workspace` between two commits is verified against each commit's own workspace, and a directory that cannot be opened for syncing after a write is reported instead of skipped.
--- .changeset/noble-hawks-drift.md
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

Inference from commits now stops with E315 in a shallow clone instead of planning a smaller bump from the history it can see. A workspace table written inline or with dotted keys is recognised as a Cargo workspace root, a pnpm workspace is published with pnpm even where its lockfile is not committed, and a nested npm workspace publishes from its own directory. An unreadable `src/bin` no longer hides a binary from `callisto init`, and the napi target check reads the main package's own `package.json` wherever it is.

A nested npm workspace that declares `workspaces` in its `package.json` and has no lockfile now publishes from its own directory, and a lockfile beside a package no longer takes it out of its workspace. `npm view` and a publish by directory run in that directory too, so the version looked for and the version published come from the same `.npmrc`. A package that moves to a different `package.workspace` between two commits is verified against each commit's own workspace, and a directory that cannot be opened for syncing after a write is reported instead of skipped.
--- .changeset/noble-hawks-drift.md
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

Inference from commits now stops with E315 in a shallow clone instead of planning a smaller bump from the history it can see. A workspace table written inline or with dotted keys is recognised as a Cargo workspace root, a pnpm workspace is published with pnpm even where its lockfile is not committed, and a nested npm workspace publishes from its own directory. An unreadable `src/bin` no longer hides a binary from `callisto init`, and the napi target check reads the main package's own `package.json` wherever it is.

# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's

# 8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit

Status: Accepted (implemented in 2c27f8d0b)

## Context

- Callisto rewrites files users own and review: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, changelogs, `pre.json`.
- `--dry-run` is a global flag; `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute` reject it (`crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`). "Respect `--dry-run`" was once a convention, and `pre enter`, `pre exit` and `init` forgot it: `pre` wrote `.changeset/pre.json` unconditionally (d15d4c2b0; `crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`).
- An interrupted run must never leave a partially written file (VER-APPLY-05, `docs/specs/versioning.json`).

## Decision

- TOML edits go through `toml_edit`, changing the existing item in place. `package.json` goes through `serde_json` with `preserve_order`, and indentation, line endings and BOM are detected on read and reproduced on write (`FormatFingerprint`). Callisto-owned JSON such as `pre.json` is regenerated canonically (`crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs`).
- Every file content write goes through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`: temp file in the target's directory, fsync, rename, then fsync the parent and grandparent. Deletions (consumed changesets, `pre.json`) and directory creation use `std::fs` directly.
- Write primitives take `&ApplyPermit`. Its only field is private; outside tests the only constructor is `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)`, which returns `None` on a dry run.

## Options considered

- **Parse into typed structs and serialize back (serde round-trip) for TOML** — reason not recorded. CM.4.1 only says editing the existing item in place, rather than replacing it, "is what makes `toml_edit` preserve comments, blank lines, key order, and inline-table formatting the caller did not touch" (docs/01-spec.md CM.4.1). JSON has no comments, so an order-preserving round trip plus fingerprint is enough (CM.5.1).
- **Regex or line-based edits** — reason not recorded. The rule appears in AGENTS.md invariant 2 without a stated reason.
- **Convention-based dry-run checks** — rejected: "A convention every new write site must remember will eventually be forgotten at one" (`permit.rs`), after `pre` and `init` did (d15d4c2b0). With a permit, a write site has nothing to pass unless its handler minted one (2c27f8d0b).

## Consequences

- TOML manifest diffs in release PRs show only version and dependency-spec changes. `package.json` is re-serialized with serde_json's pretty printer, keeping key order, indentation, line endings, BOM and trailing newline; other layout (for example an inline array) is normalized (`crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs`).
- CRLF manifests and changelogs stay CRLF.
- A failed run can leave earlier files updated; `atomic_write` only prevents a torn single file (VER-APPLY-05).
- Tests need `ApplyPermit::force_for_tests()`, behind `cfg(test)` or the `callisto-model/test-util` feature, enabled only under `[dev-dependencies]`.
- The permit is a type check only. It does not stop code that calls `std::fs` directly, and a handler can still mint one with a literal `false`: `release`, `release artifact-manifest` and `init` do so behind their own dry-run branch (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs`, `init.rs`).

## Enforcement

- Type: `ApplyPermit` (`crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs`), required by `atomic_write` (`crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs`), `Manifest::persist`, changelog writes and the release providers.
- Tests: `crates/callisto-cli/tests/dry_run_invariant_tests.rs` using `assert_no_disk_mutation` (`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/dry_run.rs`); format tests in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` and `npm.rs` (CRLF, BOM, tab indent, comment and decor preservation).

## Revisit when

- A manifest format appears that no format-preserving editor supports.
- Writes must happen outside a command handler that can read the dry-run flag.

# 2. The committed version decision is the release authority

Status: Accepted (implemented in #54)

## Context

- After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54).
- Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`).

## Decision

`callisto version --emit-decision <path>` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to `<path>`. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision <file>` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate").

## Options considered

- **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. ## Item 1 detail

**The `RewriteKey` problem.** The W10 brief (git show cc8d9b5d0) said a repeated (kind, name) declaration was untracked. Fixing that needed a discriminator on `RewriteKey`, which is a public-API change guarded by `check-api`.

- `DepLocator` is `Unspecified | Cargo{section,target} | Python{container,position}`.
- Python containers cover `[project].dependencies`, each extra, and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` [S dependency.rs:146-182].
- Cargo target tables and Python requirements declared twice are both rewritten in every place [S CHANGELOG 0.11.0].

**What was reproduced.** I built a uv workspace: core-py 0.1.0 with a minor changeset, plus app-py and pyr-py pinning `core-py>=0.1.0,<0.2` or `^0.1.0` in every table. After `callisto version`:
- Rewritten: `[project].dependencies` and `[project.optional-dependencies]` (to `>=0.2.0, <1`) [R].
- Silently skipped, with no diagnostic, still `>=0.1.0,<0.2` [R]:
  - `[dependency-groups].dev`
  - `[dependency-groups].test`
  - `[tool.uv].dev-dependencies`
- Not read at all [R]: `[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]` and `[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]`. Only `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` is read [S python.rs:497-565].
- Skipped by design, not a bug: the cascade never rewrites or cascades `DepKind::Dev` edges for any ecosystem [S cascade.rs:444]. Dev tables would stay unrewritten even if they were read, unless that rule changes.

- PEP 735 groups, uv dev-dependencies and Poetry groups are not published in wheel metadata.
- uv ignores a version pin on a `workspace = true` member. `uv lock --offline` succeeded with a stale `<0.2` group pin on a bumped member [R, py2].

**Two bugs I found on the way.**
1. A Poetry caret or tilde spec on a co-released dependency is not rewritten.
   - `python.rs::round_trip` handles only `==`, `~=`, `>=` and two-clause `>=,<`.

2. `>=0.1.0,<0.2` is rewritten to `>=0.2.0, <1` [R]. That widens the upper bound past the 0.x minor boundary.

Recommendation: fix the Poetry caret case (S to M, rewrite `^`/`~` natively) before v1. Treat dev-group tracking as a decision: document-only is cheapest.

## Item 7

Everything below is for a `package.json` that `callisto version` touches [R].
- **Preserved:**
  - key order
  - tab, 2-space and 4-space indent (mixed indent normalizes to the detected style)
  - CRLF
  - UTF-8 BOM
  - missing trailing newline
  - `1.0`, `-0.0` and integers that fit u64 (a 20-digit u64 stayed exact)
- **Changed:**
  - Inline arrays and objects are expanded one item per line, for example `["x","y"]` and `{"a":1}`.
  - `é` and `\u007f` become raw UTF-8, and `\/` becomes `/`.
  - `1e3` becomes `1000.0`. `1.5E-7` becomes `1.5e-7`.
  - `1.10` becomes `1.1`. A 30-digit integer becomes `1.2345678901234568e+29`, which is lossy. An over-precise decimal becomes `0.1`.

  - A lone surrogate escape (`\ud83d`) fails with E209. That is fail-closed, but Node accepts it.
- Only the number and duplicate-key changes can lose information. Parsed values equal what Node would read, except the duplicate-key drop and the E209 rejection.
- ADR 8 already documents "inline array normalized". AGENTS.md invariant 2 says "key order and fingerprinted indentation". Line endings, BOM and trailing newline are preserved in practice. Number and escape rewriting is undocumented.
- Fix options:
  - Document the list above (S).
  - Replace the serde round trip with a span-preserving JSON editor to avoid layout drift (L). That needs a new dependency, must still go through `atomic_write`, and invariant 2 forbids regex or line edits. The edit must be a real CST library, not text surgery.
- Recommendation: document it. Optionally enable `serde_json`'s `arbitrary_precision` (S) to stop the number loss, and file a note about E209.

## Item 9

- **Threat model (ADR 2).** The merged release commit is authorized by the reviewed merge. The decision is verified by:
  - a diff-tree check that `.callisto/release-decision.json` was added or modified in this commit
  - at least one consumed changeset
  - manifest versions matching the decision
  - claimed changelogs touched
  - the unkeyed SHA-256 digest
  The ADR itself states "Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`" [S release_decision.rs:410-437, ADR 2 Consequences]. Anyone who can merge to main can hand-author a self-consistent decision plus matching manifest edits.
- **Possible extra proof.** Attest or sign the decision in the release-PR job (OIDC or `gh attestation`) and verify it at plan time. That would need new permissions on the PR action, a wire field, and a fallback for hand-made release commits. A keyed digest would need a secret in plan-time CI, which ADR 2 and the no-secrets-in-plan policy argue against. Re-deriving the decision is the rejected alternative.
- **Value.** Marginal: whoever can merge already controls the workflow. It is not in the REQ-DX-V1 "Done when" or "Decisions still open" lists. ADR 2's own revisit triggers do not fire.
- Recommendation: not a v1 requirement. Record "existing authority is sufficient".

  - A lone surrogate escape (`\ud83d`) fails with E209. That is fail-closed, but Node accepts it.
- Only the number and duplicate-key changes can lose information. Parsed values equal what Node would read, except the duplicate-key drop and the E209 rejection.
- ADR 8 already documents "inline array normalized". AGENTS.md invariant 2 says "key order and fingerprinted indentation". Line endings, BOM and trailing newline are preserved in practice. Number and escape rewriting is undocumented.
- Fix options:
  - Document the list above (S).
  - Replace the serde round trip with a span-preserving JSON editor to avoid layout drift (L). That needs a new dependency, must still go through `atomic_write`, and invariant 2 forbids regex or line edits. The edit must be a real CST library, not text surgery.
- Recommendation: document it. Optionally enable `serde_json`'s `arbitrary_precision` (S) to stop the number loss, and file a note about E209.

## Item 9

- **Threat model (ADR 2).** The merged release commit is authorized by the reviewed merge. The decision is verified by:
  - a diff-tree check that `.callisto/release-decision.json` was added or modified in this commit
  - at least one consumed changeset
  - manifest versions matching the decision
  - claimed changelogs touched
  - the unkeyed SHA-256 digest
  The ADR itself states "Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`" [S release_decision.rs:410-437, ADR 2 Consequences]. Anyone who can merge to main can hand-author a self-consistent decision plus matching manifest edits.
- **Possible extra proof.** Attest or sign the decision in the release-PR job (OIDC or `gh attestation`) and verify it at plan time. That would need new permissions on the PR action, a wire field, and a fallback for hand-made release commits. A keyed digest would need a secret in plan-time CI, which ADR 2 and the no-secrets-in-plan policy argue against. Re-deriving the decision is the rejected alternative.
- **Value.** Marginal: whoever can merge already controls the workflow. It is not in the REQ-DX-V1 "Done when" or "Decisions still open" lists. ADR 2's own revisit triggers do not fire.
- Recommendation: not a v1 requirement. Record "existing authority is sufficient".
